paragraphs.source_en: On the second day of the sixth month in the third year of Keichō, Hideyoshi's condition worsened, leaving him unable to rise from his bed, and the news soon spread beyond the castle. By the middle of the sixth month, uncertainty had taken hold throughout Fushimi Castle. The lingering air of the age of war had yet to disperse, and now the Taikō, revered by all the people, had fallen ill again. No one could foresee how it would end.

paragraphs.source_zh: 庆长三年六月初二，秀吉病情愈重，已卧床不起，这个消息很快传到城外。至六月中旬，伏见城已是人心浮动。乱世余风尚未散尽，万民景仰的太阁又倒下了，结局到底如何，自然难以预料。

paragraphs.source_en: On the sixteenth day of the sixth month, Tokugawa Ieyasu summoned all the daimyō stationed in the capital to the great hall of Fushimi Castle and held a magnificent banquet in the Taikō's name. In truth, Hideyoshi had not sanctioned the banquet. Ieyasu had summoned the five commissioners—Maeda Gen'i, Asano Nagamasa, Mashita Nagamori, Ishida Mitsunari, and Natsuka Masaie—and all but compelled them to hold it.

paragraphs.source_zh: 六月十六，德川家康把驻京大名们都召集到伏见城大厅内，以太阁的名义举行了一次盛大的酒宴。这场酒宴其实并未得到秀吉的许可，而是家康把前田玄以、浅野长政、增田长盛、石田三成、长束正家五奉行召集起来，勉强让他们举行的。

paragraphs.source_en: “Some among the commanders now dare to slight their lord's commands. If this is allowed to continue, private feuds will break out among them and grow into open disorder. We must therefore bring them all into the castle and hold a grand banquet. I hope the five commissioners will use the occasion to admonish them properly.”

paragraphs.source_en: On the sixteenth, the commanders assembled in force, and a magnificent banquet was held. During it, the five commissioners took the floor in turn to expound upon the state of the realm, warning the commanders to set aside their private grudges and obey their lord's commands. Ieyasu sat in the place of honor beside Hideyori and Toshiie. At first he remained silent, leaving the five commissioners to conduct everything.
